issue: Do the due-process protections of U.S.S.G. § 6A1.3(a), including a defendant's right to contest factual matters reasonably in dispute, apply to sentence-reduction proceedings under 18 U.S.C. § 3582(c)(2)?

sides.position: Section 6A1.3's dispute-resolution and due-process protections apply in § 3582(c)(2) sentence-reduction proceedings, so the defendant must get notice and an opportunity to contest new information.
cases: United States v. Mueller, 168 F.3d 186 (5th Cir. 1999)
United States v. Neal, 611 F.3d 399 (7th Cir. 2010)
United States v. Foster, 575 F.3d 861 (8th Cir. 2009)
United States v. Jules (11th Cir.), 595 F.3d
United States v. Harmon, No. 24-2057 (3d Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Section 6A1.3 applies only to original sentencing proceedings, not to § 3582(c)(2) proceedings.
cases: United States v. Mercado-Moreno, 869 F.3d 942 (9th Cir. 2017)

this_court: The Third Circuit agrees with the position that § 6A1.3(a) due-process protections apply to § 3582(c)(2) sentence-reduction motions.
quote: But there is a circuit split on this issue.
cite: United States v. Paul Harmon, No. 24-2057 (3rd Cir. 2025)
